process.title: A clear website process for scoping, building and launching work that can be verified
process.intro: The section now follows the same logic buyers use when they compare a web development partner: understand the goal, build with the right stack, then launch and measure what changed.

discovery.title: Align the business goal before touching design or code
discovery.body: We start by clarifying the offer, priority pages and the search terms people are likely to use before they land on your services page or contact form.

points.goals: Define the conversion goal, decision-maker questions and what the page must make easier.
points.queries: Map internal search intent around web development, technical SEO and real-time 3D/VR services.
points.plan: Turn that into a lean page plan with headings, proof points and clear calls to action.

build.title: Write, design and ship pages that stay clear for humans and search engines
build.body: The implementation stays practical: concise copy, structure that is easy to scan, and a stack chosen for performance, maintainability and SEO-friendly delivery.

stackItems.delivery: GitHub · short PRs · visible review checkpoints

launch.title: Verify what shipped and measure whether the section earns more qualified interest
launch.body: Nothing is treated as finished just because it looks better. The launch step ties copy, code and public proof back to visible checks and follow-up measurement.

verify.body: Check headings, links, localization, linting and whether the service narrative is still easy to scan.

publish.body: Keep GitHub, ArtStation and LinkedIn connected so buyers can validate the making-of instead of relying on generic claims.

measure.body: Review whether more visitors reach the services page, use relevant internal queries or start a contact conversation after the update.

proof.title: Text-based proof beats vague claims
proof.intro: The homepage can already show how work becomes tangible: delivered project types, a named stack and public traces that are easy to verify, without waiting for new media assets.

web.title: Sites and user journeys built to convert
web.body: Web work relies on Next.js, React, TypeScript, technical SEO and short iterations to turn a brief into pages that feel sharper, more credible and easier to measure.

realtime.title: Prototypes and demos that make ideas concrete
realtime.body: Unreal, Unity and WebGL are used to show a workflow, validate an interaction or help stakeholders understand quickly what will actually be delivered.

trust.title: GitHub, ArtStation and LinkedIn as trust signals
trust.body: Instead of hiding tools and references in the footer, the homepage now connects public profiles, stack choices and delivery method to make the making-of easier to trust.
